notes.dh: או דילמא לר' יהודה חומרא הוא דאית ליה
notes.he: שהוא מחמיר יותר מרבנן דלרבנן אינה מביאה קרבן לעולם אלא על האחרון ולר' יהודה מביאה על הראשון ועל השלישי וכיון שמחמיר גבי קרבן מחמיר נמי לענין טומאה וטהרה דאין פורעין לראשון ימי טהרה כנגד ימי הטומאה דשני אלא ימי טומאה דשני לא מפסקי אלא עולין בחשבון ימי טהרה דראשון דאמרינן לענין טומאה ולד שני כמאן דליתי' דמי:
notes.en: Or perhaps Rabbi Yehuda holds a stringency: he is more stringent than the Rabbis, for according to the Rabbis she brings an offering only for the last, while according to Rabbi Yehuda she brings one for the first and for the third. And since he is stringent regarding the offering, he is stringent also regarding impurity and purity, so that we do not repay the first with days of purity corresponding to the days of impurity of the second; rather, the days of impurity of the second do not interrupt but count toward the tally of the days of purity of the first, for we say that with regard to impurity the second offspring is as though it does not exist.

messages.text: Come and hear a proof from a baraita:

In the case of a woman after childbirth, one slaughters the Paschal offering and sprinkles its blood on her account on the fourteenth of Nisan, if this occurs on the fortieth day after giving birth to a male or on the eightieth day after giving birth to a female. Although she is still impure at the time of the sacrifice, she will be able to partake of the Paschal offering on the night of the fifteenth of Nisan.

notes.he: את הפסח וזורקים עליה ביום ארבעים לזכר. קס"ד ביום מ' דימי טוהר דזכר:
notes.en: One slaughters: the Paschal offering, and sprinkles [its blood] on her account on the fortieth day for a male. [The Gemara] initially assumes: on the fortieth day of the days of purity of a male.

messages.text: Is that so? But she is still impure on the night of the fifteenth of Nisan, and she may not partake of sacrificial meat until she brings her offering on the forty-first day for a male or the eighty-first day for a female.
messages.quote: one slaughters the Paschal offering and sprinkles its blood on her account

notes.dh: והוינן בה עד כאן טמאה היא
notes.he: דמחוסרת כפרה:
notes.en: And we discussed it: until now she is impure: since she is lacking atonement.

notes.he: יולדת שוחטין את פסחה וזורקין דמו בשבילה ביום מ' לזכר וביום פ' לנקבה וקשה לר' לא מישתכח היכא הוי האי וק"ל ביום מ' לזכר וביום פ' לנקבה היכי שוחטין עלה עד כאן טמאה היא לענין קרבן דעדיין לא יצאת שעה שראויה להביא בה קרבן שאינה מביאה קרבן עד יום מ"א או עד יום פ"א:
notes.en: A woman after childbirth: one slaughters her Paschal offering and sprinkles its blood on her account on the fortieth day for a male and on the eightieth day for a female. … [A few words here are marked by the printer as unintelligible.] And it is difficult for us: on the fortieth day for a male and on the eightieth day for a female, how does one slaughter on her account? Until now she is impure with regard to the offering, since the time fit to bring the offering has not yet come, as she brings the offering only on day forty-one or eighty-one.

messages.text: In accordance with whose opinion is this baraita? It is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda, who says that the second offspring is deemed as though it does not exist. The baraita is dealing with a case where the woman gave birth to two male offspring on two consecutive days, and the fourteenth of Nisan occurred on the fortieth day after the birth of the second offspring, which is the forty-first day following the birth of the first.
messages.lead: And Rav Ḥisda said in response:

notes.dh: אמר רב חסדא הא מני ר' יהודה היא דאמר ולד שני כמאן דליתיה דמי
notes.he: ומוקים הא מתניתא ביולדת תאומים היום אחד ושני למחר דמ' דשני הוי מ"א לראשון והיום ראויה להביא קרבנה על הראשון ואשמועינן דשוחטין עליה ואפי' מחוסרת כפרה ולאחר שחיטת פסחה תביא כפרתה ותאכל לערב פסחה אלמא ולד שני כמאן דליתיה להיות מעכב עליה שתהא מונה לו וימשכו ימי טוהר שלה עד למחר:
notes.en: Rav Ḥisda said: Whose is this? It is Rabbi Yehuda, who says the second offspring is as though it does not exist: and he establishes this baraita as dealing with a woman who gave birth to twins, one today and the second tomorrow, so that the fortieth day of the second is the forty-first of the first, and today she is fit to bring her offering for the first. And it teaches us that one slaughters on her account even though she is lacking atonement, and after her Paschal offering is slaughtered she brings her atonement offering and eats of her Paschal offering in the evening. Evidently the second offspring is as though it does not exist, so that it does not hold her back by requiring her to count for it, which would extend her days of purity until the next day.

notes.he: מתניתא תניא כלומר הא ברייתא דשוחטין עליה ביום מ' מתרצתא היא והכי הויא כגון דילדה תאומים בב' ימים והאי דקתני ביום ארבעים לזכר ביום מ' לזכר שני דהוא יום מ"א לזכר ראשון ויום פ"א לנקבה ראשונית ור' יהודה היא דאמר ולד שני כמאן דליתיה דמי וכבר הוי יום מ"א הלכך שוחטין עליה דאי אמרת בטומאה סבירא ליה לר' יהודה כו':
notes.en: And Rav Ḥisda said: this baraita is to be explained, and it is like this: for example, where she gave birth to twins on two [consecutive] days, and when it teaches “on the fortieth day for a male,” it means the fortieth day of the second male, which is day forty-one of the first male, and day eighty-one of the first female. And it is Rabbi Yehuda, who says the second offspring is as though it does not exist, and it is already day forty-one; therefore one slaughters on her account. For if you say that concerning impurity Rabbi Yehuda holds, etc.

messages.text: And if you say that concerning impurity, Rabbi Yehuda holds that the second offspring is considered as though it is extant, which means that the days of purity following the first birth are delayed by the second birth and the mother does not become pure until the second term is complete, how may one slaughter the Paschal offering on her account on the fortieth day? After all, in the evening of the fifteenth she also may not eat the Paschal offering, because only forty days will have passed from the time of the second birth, and she would still be impure.

notes.dh: ואי אמרת בטומאה סבירא ליה לר' יהודה כמאן דאיתיה דמי
notes.he: לגרום ימי טומאה שלו השלמה לימי טוהר של ראשון היכי שחטינן לאורתא נמי לא מציא אכלה שהולד השני גרם להאריך ימי טוהר של ראשון יום אחד שהרי שמיני לראשון הוא שביעי לשני ומימי טומאתו הוא והפסיק מניינו של ראשון וצריכה להשלימו ועד יום מ' ושנים לראשון אינה ראויה להביא כפרתה אלא לאו ש"מ כמאן דליתא דמי ועולין ימי טומאה וטהרה שלו למנין ימי טוהר של ראשון:
notes.en: And if you say that concerning impurity Rabbi Yehuda holds that it is as though it exists: so that its days of impurity cause a completion of the days of purity of the first; how does one slaughter? In the evening, too, she could not eat it, for the second offspring caused the days of purity of the first to be extended by one day: the eighth day of the first is the seventh of the second and is one of its days of impurity, so it interrupted the count of the first, and she must complete it; and until day forty-two of the first she is not fit to bring her atonement offering. Rather, must one not conclude from it that it is as though it does not exist, and its days of impurity and purity count toward the tally of the days of purity of the first?

messages.text: Rather, must one not conclude from it that concerning ritual purity and impurity, Rabbi Yehuda holds that the second offspring is considered as though it does not exist?

notes.he: ליל פ"א שהוא פסח לא מצי אכלה דאע"ג דלמחר מתיא קרבן לילה מחוסר זמן להקרבה הוא ומחוסרת כפורים היא אלא לאו ש"מ כו':
notes.en: In the evening, too: on the night of [day] eighty-one, which is the night of Pesaḥ, she could not eat it, for even though she brings the offering the next day, at night she is still short of the time for her offering, and she is lacking atonement. Rather, must one not conclude, etc.

messages.text: Actually, I could say to you: Even concerning impurity and purity, Rabbi Yehuda holds that the second offspring is considered as something that does exist; and when that baraita is taught, it is dealing with a case of a woman who gave birth to one child, and it is referring to a case of a Paschal offering that is brought in impurity. When the majority of a community is impure, the Paschal offering is brought even in impurity.

notes.he: וההיא ברייתא לאו בולד שני מיתוקמא אלא בכל ולדות דעלמא ודקשיא לך הא לאורתא נמי מחוסרת כפורים היא בפסח הבא בטומאה עסקינן דנטמא רוב הקהל ואישתראי טומאה לגביה:
notes.en: Actually, I could say to you, etc.: and that baraita is not established as dealing with a second offspring but with any ordinary birth. And as for your difficulty that in the evening, too, she is lacking atonement: we are dealing with a Paschal offering brought in impurity, where most of the community became impure, and impurity was permitted for her.

notes.he: סבירא ליה כמאן דאיתיה דמי [ודקשיא לך] אמאי שוחטין עליה דכי תניא ההיא דשוחטין עליה בפסח הבא בטומאה דרוב צבור טמאי מתים היו ועשוהו בטומאה והואיל ובא בטומאה מצי אכלה מיניה:
notes.en: Actually: he holds that it is as though it exists. [And as for your difficulty] why one slaughters on her account: when that baraita is taught, that one slaughters on her account, it is about a Paschal offering brought in impurity, where most of the community were impure from corpses and performed it in impurity; and since it is brought in impurity, she can eat of it.

messages.text: And in that case, does she partake of it, as the baraita suggests? But didn’t we learn in a mishna (Pesaḥim 95b):
messages.quote: a Paschal offering that is brought in impurity

messages.text: With regard to a Paschal offering brought in impurity, men who experience a gonorrhea-like discharge [zavim], women who experience a discharge of uterine blood after their menstrual periods [zavot], menstruating women, and women after childbirth may not partake of it.

notes.he: דכי אישתראי טומאה בצבור לגבי טומאת מת אישתראי דכתיב (במדבר ט׳:י׳) איש כי יהיה טמא לנפש וגו' ועלה דרשינן (פסחים דף סו:) איש נדחה לפסח שני ואין צבור נדחין אלא עושין בטומאה:
notes.en: May not partake of it, etc.: for when impurity is permitted for the community, it is permitted with regard to impurity imparted by a corpse, as it is written: “If any man shall be impure by reason of a corpse” (Numbers 9:10), and on this we expound (Pesaḥim 66b): An individual is deferred to the second Pesaḥ, but a community is not deferred; rather, they perform it in impurity.

notes.he: לא יאכלו ממנו זבין וזבות נידות ויולדות דאינו נאכל בטומאה אלא לציבור טמאי מתים בלבד:
notes.en: And does she partake of it? But didn’t we learn: zavim, zavot, menstruating women and women after childbirth may not partake of it; for it is eaten in impurity only by a community impure from corpses.

messages.text: In that case, they do not partake of it because they did not immerse themselves in a ritual bath. But when that mishna is taught, that one slaughters the Paschal offering and sprinkles its blood on her account, the reason is that she had already immersed herself on the eighth day after giving birth.

notes.he: דלא פסקו מזיבה או פסקו ולא ספרו ז' ולא טבלו אבל יולדת ביום ארבעים היא טבלה בשמיני ללידתה:
notes.en: They do not partake when they did not immerse: [men and women] whose discharge had not ceased, or had ceased but who had not counted seven [clean days] and had not immersed. But a woman after childbirth, on the fortieth day, had immersed on the eighth day after her birth.

notes.he: האי דקתני לא יאכלו הימנו זבין וזבות נדות ויולדות דלא אכלי בימי טומאה בדלא טבילו כשעדין לא טבלו וכי קתני דשוחטין עליה ביום מ' משום דכבר טבלה:
notes.en: When it teaches that zavim, zavot, menstruating women and women after childbirth may not partake of it, [it means] that they do not eat in their days of impurity when they have not yet immersed. And when it teaches that one slaughters on her account on the fortieth day, it is because she has already immersed.

messages.text: If that is so, then it is from the eighth day following his birth that she is fit to eat a Paschal offering brought in impurity, and there is no reason for the baraita to specify that the offering is slaughtered on the fortieth day.

notes.he: אמאי נקט יום מ' לזכר או שמונים לנקבה משמיני ללידתה נמי חזיא:
notes.en: If that is so: why does it mention the fortieth day for a male or the eightieth for a female? From the eighth day after her birth she is also fit.

messages.text: Actually, she is not fit from the eighth day, because the tanna maintains that a zav who immersed that day and is waiting for nightfall for the purification process to be completed is considered to have the status of a zav and may not partake of a Paschal offering brought in ritual impurity. Similarly, a woman who immerses after giving birth is considered like one who immersed that day, and therefore she cannot partake of sacrificial meat until the end of the forty-day period.

notes.he: דטבילה גורמת משמיני דילה כשטבלה בו חזיא למשחט עליה ואמאי נקט יום מ' משום דכבר טבלה לזכר לא משמיני ועד מ' לא חזיא למשחט עליה דקסבר טבול יום דזב כזב גמור דמי דלא מצי למישחט עליה עד העריב שמשו הכא נמי טבול יום דיולדת כיולדת דמיא משמיני ועד יום מ' הוי כיומא אריכא והיינו טבול יום ארוך דאמר במס' נדה. ולא חשיב לה הערב שמש עד יום מ' לערב:
notes.en: If so: that immersion is effective, then from her eighth day, when she immersed, she is fit for one to slaughter on her account; why does it mention the fortieth day, [if the reason is] that she had already immersed? [It answers:] for a male, not from the eighth: until the fortieth she is not fit for one to slaughter on her account, since it holds that a zav who immersed that day is considered a full zav, so that one cannot slaughter on his account until his sun has set. Here, too, a woman after childbirth who immersed that day is like a woman after childbirth: from the eighth until the fortieth day is like one long day, and this is the “long tevul yom” mentioned in tractate Niddah. And sunset is not considered [to have come] for her until the evening of the fortieth day.

messages.text: If that is so, then on the fortieth day she is also not fit to eat the Paschal offering.

notes.he: אפי' לאורתא דהא מיחסרא כפרה וקס"ד מחוסר כפורים דזב כזב דמי ואינו אוכל בפסח הבא בטומאה:
notes.en: On the fortieth day she is also not fit: even in the evening, since she is lacking atonement. And at this point it is assumed that a zav who is lacking atonement is considered a zav and does not eat of a Paschal offering brought in impurity.

notes.he: אי הכי ביום מ' נמי לא חזיא למיכל לאורתא דהא מחסרא כפרה:
notes.en: If so, on the fortieth day she is also not fit to eat in the evening, since she is lacking atonement.

messages.text: This is not so; on the fortieth day she is fit to partake of the Paschal offering after nightfall, because the tanna holds that a zav who has immersed himself and waited for nightfall but is lacking atonement, i.e., he has not yet brought an atonement offering to complete the purification process, is not considered to have the status of a zav. Therefore, after completing the purification period, the woman may partake of the offering, despite the fact that she has not yet brought her atonement offering.

notes.he: לאורתא דקסבר מחוסר כפורים (דכזב) [דזב] לא כזב דמי ומצי שחיט עליה אף מחוסר כפורים דיולדת נמי:
notes.en: No, on the fortieth day she is fit: in the evening, since it holds that a zav lacking atonement is not considered a zav, and one can slaughter on his account; so too a woman after childbirth lacking atonement.

messages.text: But according to Rava, who says that a zav who is lacking atonement is considered to have the status of a zav, how does he resolve the problem in this baraita?
messages.quote: a zav who has immersed himself and waited for nightfall but is lacking atonement is not considered to have the status of a zav

notes.he: הא דרבא בשחיטת קדשים בתחילת פ"ב (דף יז:):
notes.en: This statement of Rava is in [tractate] Sheḥitat Kodashim [Zevaḥim], at the beginning of the second chapter (17b).

notes.he: במסכת זבחים מחוסר כפורים דזב כזב דמי היכי מתריץ לה ביום מ' לזכר:
notes.en: And according to Rava, who says in tractate Zevaḥim that a zav lacking atonement is considered a zav, how does he resolve “on the fortieth day for a male”?

messages.text: Rava resolves it as follows: The baraita is not referring to the fortieth day after the birth of a male, but to a miscarriage that occurred on the fortieth day after the conception of a male, or the eightieth day after the conception of a female. And it is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yishmael, who says that it takes forty-one days for a male fetus to be formed, and eighty-one days for a female fetus to be formed. Since the miscarriage occurred before the forty-first or eighty-first day, it does not render the woman impure with the impurity of childbirth, and therefore she may partake of the Paschal offering.

notes.he: לא מתרץ לה ביום מ' דימי טוהר כלל אלא הכי מוקים לה ביולדת ביום מ' להריונה וילדה זכר שוחטין עליה בו ביום ור' ישמעאל היא דאמר בפרק המפלת חתיכה (נדה ל.) בריית נקבה לפ"א:
notes.en: Rav Ashi said: Rava does not resolve it as the fortieth day of the days of purity at all. Rather, he establishes it as a woman who gave birth on the fortieth day of her pregnancy and bore a male: one slaughters on her account on that very day. And it is Rabbi Yishmael, who says in the chapter HaMappelet Ḥatikha (Niddah 30a): The formation of a female is on the eighty-first day.

notes.he: אף שאין יכולין לידע יום ארבעים ליצירה דהלא שכבת זרע שוהה לקלוט פעמים עד שלשה ימים ומיהו שמואל היה בקי כדאמרינן פרק המפלת (נדה כה:) שאני שמואל דרב גובריה:
notes.en: On the fortieth day of the formation of a male: even though one cannot know the fortieth day of formation, since semen sometimes takes up to three days to be absorbed. But Shmuel was expert in this, as we say in the chapter HaMappelet (Niddah 25b): Shmuel is different, as his ability was great.

notes.he: שוחטין עליה ביום מ' ליצירת זכר כלומר אם מיום שטבלה ונתעברה והפילה ליום מ' שיש לחוש ליצירת זכר שאם היתה מפלת למחר ליום מ"א ואם היה זכר היתה צורתו ניכרת כר' ישמעאל דאמר דזכר נגמרת ליום מ"א ונקבה לפ"א ועכשיו כיון שהפילה יום אחד קודם גמר הצורה לא חשיב ולד הילכך שוחטין עליה כשהפילה ביום מ' ליצירת זכר או ביום פ' ליצירת נקבה:
notes.en: Rava resolves it: one slaughters on her account on the fortieth day of the formation of a male. That is, if, from the day she immersed and conceived, she miscarried on the fortieth day, when there is concern about the formation of a male: had she miscarried the next day, on day forty-one, and it was a male, its form would be recognizable, according to Rabbi Yishmael, who says a male is complete on day forty-one and a female on day eighty-one. Now, since she miscarried one day before its form was complete, it is not considered an offspring. Therefore one slaughters on her account when she miscarried on the fortieth day of the formation of a male or on the eightieth of the formation of a female.

messages.text: But ultimately, one should conclude that she is impure because she has the status of a menstruating woman.

notes.he: אמאי שוחטין עליה בשהפילה ביום מ' תיפוק לי דאין שוחטין בטומאה משום נדה דכל יולדת נדה היא:
notes.en: Ultimately: why does one slaughter on her account when she miscarried on day forty? Let me derive [that one does not], since one does not slaughter [on her account] in impurity because she is menstruating, as every woman after childbirth is a menstruating woman.

messages.text: The mishna was stated with regard to the case of a dry birth, in which no blood was expelled, and therefore no impurity imparted.

notes.he: בלא דם:
notes.en: Dry [yavashta]: without blood.

notes.he: שלא היה בה דם כלל:
notes.en: In a dry birth: in which there was no blood at all.

messages.text: If that is so, then what is the purpose of stating it? The ruling in such a case is obvious.

notes.he: אי הכי דליכא דם פשיטא דשוחטין:
notes.en: If so, that there is no blood, it is obvious that one slaughters [on her account].

messages.text: It was necessary to state it, lest you say that it is impossible for the womb to open without blood being expelled. The tanna therefore teaches us that it is possible for the womb to open without blood being expelled. Accordingly, Rabbi Yehuda’s opinion with regard to the impurity of a second birth cannot be deduced from this mishna.

notes.he: רחם:
notes.en: The “grave” [hakever]: the womb. [The Aramaic says “the opening of the grave”; the Davidson renders it “the womb.”]

notes.dh: אי אפשר לפתיחת הקבר בלא דם
notes.he: תימה א"כ למאי איצטריך למיכתב גבי זכר וטמאה ז' ימים ואומר רבי דאי לאו קרא ה"א תטמא שבועיים מק"ו מנקבה דטהרתה מרובה ואפ"ה שבועיים כ"ש זכר שהוא מועט וכה"ג איכא בת"כ:
notes.en: It is impossible for the womb to open without blood: This is puzzling: if so, why was it necessary to write regarding a male, “and she shall be impure seven days”? And Rabbi [our teacher] says: if not for the verse, I would have said that she is impure for two weeks, by an a fortiori inference from a female: if for a female, whose purification is great, it is still two weeks, all the more so for a male, whose [purification] is small. And there is something similar in the Torat Kohanim.

notes.he: פירוש אפשר לפתיחת הקבר בלא דם והכי פסיק בשאלתות דרב אחאי מהאי דהכא מדשוחטין וזורקין:
notes.en: It teaches us: that is, it is possible for the womb to open without blood. And so it is ruled in the She’iltot of Rav Aḥai, on the basis of this passage, from “one slaughters and sprinkles.”

notes.dh: מהו דתימא אי אפשר לפתיחת הקבר בלא דם
notes.he: וראתה דם ואיבדתו:
notes.en: Lest you say it is impossible for the womb to open without blood: and she saw blood and it was lost.

notes.he: קמ"ל דאפשר לפתיחת הקבר בלא דם:
notes.en: It teaches us that it is possible for the womb to open without blood.

messages.text: Come and hear a proof from a baraita:

The verse states with regard to a woman who gave birth to a female: “And she shall continue in the blood of purification sixty days and six days” (Leviticus 12:5). One might have thought that she counts the days whether they are continuous or dispersed. Therefore, the verse states: “Sixty days and six days,” to teach that just as a day is a continuous time period, so too all sixty days are continuous.

verse.he: וְאִם־נְקֵבָה תֵלֵד וְטָמְאָה שְׁבֻעַיִם כְּנִדָּתָהּ וְשִׁשִּׁים יוֹם וְשֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים תֵּשֵׁב עַל־דְּמֵי טׇהֳרָהֿ׃
verse.en: If she bears a female, she shall be impure two weeks as during her menstruation, and she shall remain in a state of blood purification for sixty-six days.

notes.he: כגון שלא הפילה בינתיים:
notes.en: One might have thought: whether continuous: for example, where she did not miscarry in the meantime.

notes.he: כגון אם הפילה לסוף נ"ד יכול יפסיקו לה טומאת הנפל וישלימו לה ששים יום של טהרה ללידה הראשונה לבד מימי טומאת הנפל המפסיקין בינתיים:
notes.en: Or dispersed: for example, if she miscarried at the end of fifty-four [days], one might have thought that the impurity of the miscarriage interrupts for her, and they complete for her sixty days of purity for the first birth, apart from the days of impurity of the miscarriage that interrupt in between.

notes.dh: תלמוד לומר יום מה יום כולו רצוף
notes.he: אם טמא טמא ואם טהור טהור אף ששים יום כולם רצופים לטהרה:
notes.en: The verse states “day”: just as a day is entirely continuous, if impure, impure, and if pure, pure, so too the sixty days are all continuous for purity.

notes.he: (כולן) כולן ששים בלא הפסק והוא חומרא דהיינו כגון שילדה נקבה וחזרה והפילה בתוך ימי טהרתה של ראשונה ובאו ימי טומאה של שני בתוך ימי טהרה של ראשון. אי אמרינן ששים בעינן רצופין עולין ימי טומאה של שני בחשבון הששים ונפחתו בימי טהרה של ראשון:
notes.en: One might have thought: whether continuous: all sixty without interruption, and that is a stringency. For example, she gave birth to a female and then miscarried again within the days of purity of the first, so that the days of impurity of the second fell within the days of purity of the first. If we say that we need sixty continuous days, the days of impurity of the second count toward the sixty and are taken off the days of purity of the first.

notes.he: או יכול ששים בין מפוזרים היינו לקולא כלומר שמפסיקין ימי טומאה של שני ימי טהרה של ראשון וחוזרין ומשלימין ימי טהרה דראשון לאחר ימי טומאה דשני ואינה מפסדת כלום מימי טהרה:
notes.en: Or one might have thought, sixty whether dispersed: that is a leniency, that is, the days of impurity of the second interrupt the days of purity of the first, and afterward they complete the days of purity of the first after the days of impurity of the second, and she loses nothing of her days of purity.

notes.dh: ת"ל יום מה יום כולו רצוף אף ששים כולן רצופין
notes.he: כלומר דאין משלימין לאחר מיכן:
notes.en: The verse states “day”: just as a day is entirely continuous, so too the sixty are all continuous; that is, they are not completed afterward.

messages.text: And whose opinion is this? If we say it is the opinion of the Rabbis, that cannot be correct, as are the Rabbis of the opinion that it is possible for a woman who gave birth to count dispersed days? This is not the case, as the Rabbis count the days of purification from the second birth.

notes.he: הא מוולד שני מניא ולא משלמו ימי טוהר דראשון אלא אחר אחרון הולכין הלכך לא משכחת להו מפוזרין לעולם:
notes.en: Do they hold of dispersed days? But she counts from the second offspring, and they do not complete the days of purity of the first; rather, they follow the last one. Therefore, according to them, you never find dispersed days.

notes.he: כלל והא אמרי לעולם דמוולד שני מונה אלמא לרבנן לעולם רצופין הוו דאין בהן שום הפסק:
notes.en: Do the Rabbis hold of dispersed days at all? But they say that she always counts from the second offspring; evidently, according to the Rabbis, the days are always continuous, with no interruption.

messages.text: Rather, is it not the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda? And from the fact that he prescribes for her sixty continuous days to be counted together, conclude from it that Rabbi Yehuda maintains that the second offspring is considered extant only where a stringency results, but where a leniency results, in that she continues counting the days of purity of the first birth after completing the days of impurity for the second birth, he does not maintain that the second offspring is considered as though it exists.

notes.he: דאית ליה ימי טוהר דראשון דלדידיה ראשון עיקר לענין קרבן ואשמועי' הכא דלענין טומאה וטהרה לית ליה ימי טוהר לראשון דא"כ לא משכחת לה טהורין רצופין אלא משני מניא וש"מ חומרא בעלמא אית ליה במתני' לאפושי קרבנות ולענין קרבן לחודיה הוא דמני לראשון אבל לגבי טומאה להשלים ימי טוהר לראשון למנותן מפוזרין לית ליה דקולא היא דהדר בעיא למיתב ימי טוהר לשני:
notes.en: Rather, is it not Rabbi Yehuda: who holds that there are days of purity for the first, since according to him the first is the principal one with regard to the offering. And it teaches us here that with regard to impurity and purity he does not hold that there are [completed] days of purity for the first, for if so you would not find continuous days of purity for her; rather, she counts from the second. And conclude from it that he merely holds a stringency in the mishna, to increase offerings, and only with regard to the offering does she count for the first; but with regard to impurity, completing the days of purity of the first by counting them dispersed, he does not hold this, since it is a leniency, as she would again need to assign days of purity to the second.

notes.he: דליכא למימר רצופין היינו כימי ספורו של זב שלא יהא טומאה מפסיק ביניהם ה"נ ל"ג יום יהיו נקיים דכתיב תשב על דמי טהרה אלמא דאין צריכין נקיים:
notes.en: Conclude from it a stringency, etc.: for one cannot say that “continuous” is like the days of counting of a zav, that no impurity may interrupt between them, so that here, too, the thirty-three days would have to be clean [of blood], since it is written: “She shall continue in the blood of purification”; evidently they need not be clean.

notes.he: דאמר מוולד ראשון מונה ולטעמיה קא יכיל למיבעי אי רצופין אי מפוזרין ומדקא יהיב ששים רצופין בהדדי דקאמר מה יום כולו רצוף ש"מ לחומרא אית ליה דימי טומאה דשני עולין בחשבון ששים דראשון:
notes.en: Rather, is it not Rabbi Yehuda: who says she counts from the first offspring; and according to his reasoning one can ask whether they are continuous or dispersed. And since it gives sixty continuous days together, as it says, “just as a day is entirely continuous,” conclude from it that he holds a stringency: the days of impurity of the second count toward the sixty of the first.

messages.text: No, actually, the baraita is stated in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis. And what are we dealing with here? We are dealing with a woman who gives birth to a male within the eighty-day period following the birth of a female, so that the forty-day period for the male is entirely subsumed within the purification period for the female.

notes.he: וה"ד מפוזרין ביולדת זכר בתוך שמונים של נקבה שימי טוהר של זכר כלין קודם לשמונים דנקבה ראשונה ובכה"ג דימי טוהר של שני כלין קודם לימי טוהר דראשון לית להו לרבנן דמוולד שני לימנו ובעיא לאשלומי ימי טוהר דראשון ואתא קרא לאשמועינן דלא משלימין לבתר פ' דלידה ראשונה שבעה כנגד ז' ימי טומאה דזכר שהפסיקו בינתיים אלא משני מונה:
notes.en: Actually, it is the Rabbis: and this is how you find dispersed days: a woman who gave birth to a male within the eighty [days] of a female, where the days of purity of the male end before the eighty of the first female. In a case like this, where the days of purity of the second end before the days of purity of the first, the Rabbis do not hold that she counts from the second offspring, and she must complete the days of purity of the first. And the verse comes to teach us that she does not complete, after the eighty of the first birth, seven [days] corresponding to the seven days of impurity of the male that interrupted in between; rather, she counts from the second.

notes.he: לעולם רבנן היא ודקא אמרת מי אית להו מפוזרין כלל הכא במאי עסקינן דילדה זכר ביום פ' של נקבה שימי טהרתה של נקבה מושכין לאחר ימי טהרתה של זכר דימי טהרתה דזכר ל"ג ודנקבה ס"ו מהו דתימא כי אמרו רבנן דביטל שני הראשון הני מילי כשמושכין ימי טהרתה של שני לאחר ימי טהרתה של ראשון אבל הכא דימי טהרה דראשון מושכין לאחר טהרה [של] שני אמרינן דאית בהו דין מפוזרין דמשלימין לאחר ימי טומאה דשני ימי טהרה דראשון:
notes.en: Actually, it is the Rabbis; and as for your saying, do they hold of dispersed days at all? What are we dealing with here? Where she gave birth to a male in the eighty [days] of a female, so that the days of purity of the female extend beyond the days of purity of the male, since the days of purity of a male are thirty-three and of a female sixty-six. Lest you say that when the Rabbis said the second voids the first, that applies only where the days of purity of the second extend beyond those of the first; but here, where the days of purity of the first extend beyond those of the second, we say that the law of dispersed days applies, and the days of purity of the first are completed after the days of impurity of the second.

messages.text: In such a case, even the Rabbis would maintain that the second birth does not interrupt the term following the first. She would observe the seven days of impurity for the male, and then complete the days of purity for the female. Consequently, the verse teaches that the sixty-six days of purity following the first birth are observed continuously, and there is no need to observe additional days due to the intervening days of impurity.

But ultimately, this scenario is impossible; the reason is that the days of the first birth are completed while the days of the latter birth are not completed, as the Rabbis count the days following the second birth, and therefore the term relating to the first birth is abandoned.
messages.quote: a woman who gives birth to a male within the eighty-day period following the birth of a female

notes.he: לא משכחת הכי דשלמין שמונים דנקבה קמייתא ועד כאן מ' דזכר לא שלמין דלא משכחת לידת זכר עד נ"ד דנקבה י"ד דטומאה דנקבה ומ' דיצירת הזכר וכיון (דרבינן לוולד שני משום דלא) משכחת מפוזרין:
notes.en: Ultimately: you do not find such a case, that the eighty of the first female are complete while the forty of the male are not yet complete, for you cannot find the birth of a male before [day] fifty-four of the female: fourteen of the female’s impurity and forty for the formation of the male. And since … [a few words here are in parentheses in the printed text and are unclear] … you do not find dispersed days.

notes.he: מי מצית אמרת הכי הא לעולם שלמין ימי טהרה דקדמאה ועד כען בתראה לא שלמי ובהא היכא דימי טהרה דשני מושכין לאחר ימי טהרה דראשון רבנן לולד שני מנו. והכא ימי טהרה דשני משכי שפי' מן קדמאי כיצד נתעברה זכר לאחר י"ד ימי טומאה דנקבה והפילה למ"א נשתיירו מן ס"ו ימי טהרה דנקבה כ"ה ימים וימי טהרה דזכר מושכין עד מ' יום ובהא קסברי רבנן דביטל שני הראשון והיכי משכחת מפוזרין לרבנן:
notes.en: Ultimately: can you really say this? The days of purity of the first are always complete while those of the latter are not yet complete; and where the days of purity of the second extend beyond those of the first, the Rabbis count for the second offspring. And here the days of purity of the second extend well beyond the first. How so? If she conceived a male after the fourteen days of impurity of the female and miscarried at forty-one [days], there remained twenty-five of the female’s sixty-six days of purity, while the male’s days of purity extend for forty days. In such a case the Rabbis hold that the second voids the first. So how do you find dispersed days according to the Rabbis?

messages.text: Rather, you find a case of counting dispersed days according to the Rabbis in a case where a woman gives birth to twins, first a female and then a male, and for example, she gives birth to the latter offspring, the male, on the twentieth day of the days of purity for the female, as she is required to observe for him seven days of impurity for birth.
messages.lead: The Gemara offers a different explanation of the baraita:

notes.he: שנתעברו:
notes.en: With a woman who gives birth to twins: who were conceived [together].

notes.he: עשרים לאו דוקא דהוא הדין לבציר מהכי או טפי מהכי:
notes.en: On the twentieth of the days of purity: twenty is not precise; the same applies to fewer than this or more than this.

notes.he: אלא משכחת לה לרבנן כגון ביולדת תאומים אחד נקבה אחד זכר וילדה נקבה קודם ואח"כ נשתהא הזכר במעי אמו עד עשרים יום לימי טהרה של נקבה ונולד ביום עשרין ועדיין לאחר לידת הזכר נשתיירו מ"ז ימי טהרה לנקבה ויום עשרים שהוא של לידה חושב בכלל:
notes.en: Rather, you find it according to the Rabbis, for example, with a woman who gives birth to twins, one female and one male: she bore the female first, and afterward the male lingered in his mother’s womb until the twentieth of the female’s days of purity and was born on day twenty. After the birth of the male there still remained forty-seven days of purity for the female, the twentieth day, the day of the birth, being counted in the total.

notes.he: ובעיא למינקט לזכר ז' ימי טומאה דלידה בתוך הנך מ"ז ימי טהרה שנשתיירו לנקבה וכאן מושכין ימי טהרה דנקבה ז' יום לאחר ימי טהרה דזכר והכא לא מצי למימר ביטל שני את הראשון דימי טהרה דראשון מאוחרין:
notes.en: And she must take for the male seven days of impurity of birth within those forty-seven days of purity remaining for the female. Here the female’s days of purity extend seven days beyond the male’s days of purity, and one cannot say here that the second voided the first, since the days of purity of the first come later.

messages.text: And this is what the baraita is saying: One might have thought that where she gave birth to twins, a female initially and a male afterward, that the impurity of the second birth interrupts the term following the first birth in the middle, and she counts sixty-six dispersed days. Therefore, the verse states: “Sixty days and six days,” to teach that just as a day is an entirely continuous time period, so too all sixty days are to be continuous. Since the baraita could be in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis, no proof can be inferred with regard to the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda.

notes.he: כלומר שפסקו לה שבעה ימי טומאה דזכר לימי טוהר דנקבה וליתיב לה שבעה אחריני לאחר שמונים ללידה הראשונה ת"ל יום:
notes.en: Dispersed: that is, that the seven days of impurity of the male interrupted the days of purity of the female, and we would give her seven others after the eighty of the first birth. The verse states “day.”

notes.dh: והכי קאמר יכול היכא דילדה תאומים נקבה מעיקרא וזכר לבסוף
notes.he: לאחר כ' יום של טהרה אימא תיפסוק טומאה דלידה זכר במיצעי ונימני להו ששים וששה מפוזרין כלומר י"ד ימים לאחר מ' דזכר דשבעה שנשתיירו לנקבה לאחר ימי טהרה דזכר ועוד ז' ימים משלימין לה מפני ז' ימי טומאה דלידה זכר שהפסיקום והיינו מפוזרין (דאינין) [דאינן] מפסיקין ימי טהרה (דאינן אין):
notes.en: And this is what it is saying: one might have thought, where she bore twins, a female first and a male last, after twenty days of purity, say that the impurity of the male’s birth interrupts in the middle and we count for her sixty-six dispersed days: that is, fourteen days after the forty of the male, seven that remained for the female after the male’s days of purity and another seven days completed for her because of the seven days of impurity of the male’s birth that interrupted them. And this is “dispersed” … [the end of the sentence is garbled in the printed text].

messages.text: Come and hear a proof from a baraita which discusses a woman who gave birth to a male.

The verse states: “And she shall continue in the blood of purification three days and thirty days” (Leviticus 12:4). One might have thought that she counts the days whether they are continuous or dispersed. Therefore, the verse states: “Three days and thirty days,” to teach that just as a day is an entirely continuous time period, so too all thirty days are to be continuous.

verse.he: וּשְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם וּשְׁלֹשֶׁת יָמִים תֵּשֵׁב בִּדְמֵי טׇהֳרָהֿ בְּכׇל־קֹדֶשׁ לֹא־תִגָּע וְאֶל־הַמִּקְדָּשׁ לֹא תָבֹא עַד־מְלֹאת יְמֵי טׇהֳרָהּ׃
verse.en: She shall remain in a state of blood purification uncertain. for thirty-three days: she shall not touch any consecrated thing, nor enter the sanctuary until her period of purification is completed.

notes.he: כגון יולדת תאומים וילדה שני בתוך ל' דזכר ראשון יכול יתנו לה שבעה לבד מ' ללידה הראשונה כגון ז' ימי טומאה דשני דהשתא הוו ל' מפוזרין שהרי הפסיקו ימי טומאה בינתיים שלא עלו למנין:
notes.en: The thirty of a male, dispersed: for example, a woman who gave birth to twins and bore the second within the thirty of the first, a male. One might have thought that they give her seven [days] beyond the forty of the first birth, corresponding to the seven days of impurity of the second, so that now the thirty are dispersed, since the days of impurity interrupted in between and did not count toward the tally.

notes.he: דמפסקי והא מיירי כגון שילדה תאומים זה ביום ראשון ואחד ביום שני שסוף ימי טומאה דשני נכנס ביום טהרה דראשון וקא בעי אי משלימין אותו יום טהרה דראשון שטימאו השני אי לא וקאמר ת"ל יום דכולן רצופין וש"מ חומרא אית ליה לר' יהודה דרצופין:
notes.en: One might have thought, dispersed: that they interrupt. This is speaking, for example, where she bore twins, one on the first day and one on the second day, so that the end of the days of impurity of the second enters a day of purity of the first. It asks whether one completes that day of purity of the first that the second rendered impure, or not; and it says: the verse states “day,” that they are all continuous. And conclude from it that Rabbi Yehuda holds a stringency, that they are continuous.

messages.text: And whose opinion is this? If we say it is the Rabbis, that cannot be correct, as are the Rabbis of the opinion that
it is possible for a woman who gave birth to count dispersed days? No, as the Rabbis say that she counts the days from the birth of the second fetus.

notes.dh: מי אית להו מפוזרין הא לולד שני מנו
notes.he: וכיון דבראשון זכר ליכא לאוקומי כדאוקמא ליה דימי טוהר דראשון משכין לבתר ימי טוהר דשני:
notes.en: Do they hold of dispersed days? But they count for the second offspring: and since the first is a male, one cannot explain it as it was explained [above], that the days of purity of the first extend beyond the days of purity of the second.

messages.text: Rather, is it not the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda? And therefore, conclude from it that Rabbi Yehuda is of the opinion that the second offspring is considered as though it exists only where a stringency results, but where a leniency results, he is not of the opinion that the second offspring is considered to have existed.

notes.he: דמונה לראשון וקאמר דרצופין יהבינן לה אלמא משני הוא דמני:
notes.en: Rather, is it not Rabbi Yehuda: who counts for the first, and it says that we give her continuous days; evidently she counts from the second.

notes.dh: וש"מ חומרא אית ליה קולא לית ליה
notes.he: להאריך ימי טוהר דראשון שהשלימו לז' אחרים כנגד ז' ימי טומאה והדר מותיב ימי טוהר לשני דקולא יתירא היא:
notes.en: And conclude from it that he holds a stringency but not a leniency: to extend the days of purity of the first by completing seven others corresponding to the seven days of impurity, and then to assign days of purity to the second as well, which is an excessive leniency.

messages.text: Come and hear a proof from a baraita, which discusses the verse: “Sixty days and six days” (Leviticus 12:5).

verse.he: וְאִם־נְקֵבָה תֵלֵד וְטָמְאָה שְׁבֻעַיִם כְּנִדָּתָהּ וְשִׁשִּׁים יוֹם וְשֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים תֵּשֵׁב עַל־דְּמֵי טׇהֳרָהֿ׃
verse.en: If she bears a female, she shall be impure two weeks as during her menstruation, and she shall remain in a state of blood purification for sixty-six days.

messages.text: One might have thought that she counts these six days whether they are continuous or dispersed, so that if, for example, she miscarried on the sixty-third day, she would complete the remaining three days of purity for the first fetus after completing the period of purification for the second. Therefore, the verse states: “Sixty” to teach that just as the sixty days are all continuous, so too, the six days are all continuous.

notes.he: כגון הפילה לאחר ס"ג דטוהר דנקבה שהן ע"ז ללידתה והיה לה למנות עוד ג' ימים והפילה ונטמאו יכול יתנו לה ג' אחרים כנגד ג' אלה דנטמאו דנהוו ו' מפוזרים דהכא לא כתיב יום אלא ימים דמשמע אפילו מפוזרין:
notes.en: Six days, etc.: for example, she miscarried after sixty-three [days] of the purity of a female, which are seventy-seven from her birth, when she still had three more days to count; she miscarried, and they became impure. One might have thought that they give her three others corresponding to the three that became impure, so that the six would be dispersed, since here “day” is not written but “days,” which implies even dispersed.

notes.he: ועוד ת"ש ששת ימים והא מיירי כגון דילדה נקבה ואח"כ הפילה באותן ששת ימי טהרה שיתרין על ששים ונטמאו אותן ששת ימי טהרה וקא בעי יכול אותן ששת ימים אי בעינן להו רצופין עם ששים ומפסידתן שנטמאו או מפוזרין דמשלימין אותן לאחר ימי טומאה דשני ת"ל ששים מה ששים כולן רצופין דכתיב בהו יום אף ששה נמי:
notes.en: [Printed with an editor’s marker: “up to here belongs to 10a.”] And further, come and hear: “six days.” This is speaking, for example, where she bore a female and afterward miscarried during the six days of purity that are beyond the sixty, so that those six days of purity became impure. It asks: one might have thought, regarding those six days, whether we need them continuous with the sixty, so that she loses them because they became impure, or dispersed, so that they are completed after the days of impurity of the second. The verse states “sixty”: just as the sixty are all continuous, since “day” is written of them, so too the six.

messages.text: Whose opinion is this? If we say it is the opinion of the Rabbis, that cannot be correct, as are the Rabbis of the opinion that it is possible for a woman who gave birth to count dispersed days? Didn’t the Rabbis say that she counts for the second offspring?

notes.dh: מי אית להו מפוזרין הא לולד שני מנו
notes.he: וימי ולד שני זה מושכין ימים רבים אחר פ' של נקבה ראשונה ומפוזרין לא משכחת לה אלא לאו ר' יהודה היא כו':
notes.en: Do they hold of dispersed days? But they count for the second offspring: and the days of this second offspring extend many days beyond the eighty of the first, a female, and you do not find dispersed days. Rather, is it not Rabbi Yehuda, etc.

notes.he: מני אילימא רבנן כו':
notes.en: Whose is it? If we say the Rabbis, etc.

messages.text: Rather, is it not the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda? And therefore, may one conclude from it that Rabbi Yehuda is of the opinion that the second offspring is considered extant only where a stringency results; but where a leniency results, he is not of the opinion that the second offspring is considered to have existed?
Indeed, conclude from it that this is the case.
messages.quote: a stringency results; but where a leniency results, he is not of the opinion

messages.text: Mishna

These are the five situations mentioned in the mishna (9a) in which one brings a sliding-scale offering: For hearing the voice of an oath, i.e., where one took a false oath that he does not have any testimony to provide on a given issue; and for the utterance of the lips, which is a case where one took a false oath about a different matter;

notes.he: ושמעה קול אלה:
notes.en: MISHNA: The hearing of the voice: “and he heard the voice of adjuration” (Leviticus 5:1).

messages.text: and for the defiling of the Temple, by entering it while ritually impure, or defiling its sacrificial foods, by partaking of them while ritually impure; and a woman after childbirth; and a leper at the end of his purification process.

notes.he: בשוגג ובטוי שפתים כולהו כתיבי בהדדי בפרשת ויקרא גבי קרבן עולה ויורד דהא קרא דאו נפש כי תגע בכל דבר טמא וגו' בטומאת מקדש וקדשיו משתעי כדמפרש בפרק קמא דשבועות (דף ז.):
notes.en: And the defiling of the Temple: unwittingly; and the utterance of the lips: all of them are written together in the portion of Vayikra concerning the sliding-scale offering, for the verse “Or if a person touches any impure thing,” etc., speaks of the defiling of the Temple and its sacred foods, as explained in the first chapter of Shevuot (7a).

notes.he: הכא מני להו בחדא ובפ"ק מני להו בתרתי דהתם בכרת הוו תרי דכתיב כרת בכל חד וחד אבל הכא בקרבן דכתיב תרווייהו בכרת אחד:
notes.en: The defiling of the Temple and its sacred foods: here it counts them as one, and in the first chapter it counts them as two. For there, with regard to karet, they are two, since karet is written for each one; but here, with regard to the offering, both are written with a single karet.

notes.dh: אלו מביאין קרבן עולה ויורד כו' ועל טומאת מקדש וקדשיו
notes.he: הכא קתני גבי קרבן קא חשיב לטומאה מקדש וקדשיו בחדא אבל בפירקין קמא גבי כרת קא חשיב להו בתרתי דבתרוויהו כתב בהו כרת והכא גבי קדשים אמאי חשיב להו בחדא דהכי אמרינן התם במסכת שבועות הזהיר וענש על הטומאה וחייב קרבן על הטומאה דכתיב ונפש כי תגע בכל טמא בטומאת אדם כו' מה כשהזהיר וענש לא ענש אלא על טומאת מקדש וקדשיו דכתיב בכל קדש לא תגע וכתב בהו כרת אף חיוב קרבן אלא על
notes.en: These bring a sliding-scale offering, etc., and for the defiling of the Temple and its sacred foods: here, with regard to the offering, it counts the defiling of the Temple and its sacred foods as one, but in our first chapter, with regard to karet, it counts them as two, since karet is written for each of them. And here, with regard to sacred foods [an editor’s note suggests reading: with regard to the offering], where only one offering is written for both of them, it counts them as one. Why does it count them as one? For so we say there, in tractate Shevuot: He warned and punished concerning impurity, and imposed an offering concerning impurity, as it is written: “Or if a person touches any impure thing,” with human impurity, etc. Just as when He warned and punished, He punished only for the defiling of the Temple and its sacred foods, as it is written: “She shall touch no hallowed thing,” and He wrote karet for them, so too, the obligation of an offering is only for

notes.he: טומאת מקדש וקדשיו:
notes.en: the defiling of the Temple and its sacred foods.

messages.text: Gemara

There is a case in which one brings the offering in one of two possible states, either a bird offering if the individual is in a state of poverty or an animal offering if he is in a state of wealth; and there is a case in which one brings the offering in one of three possible states, of wealth, of poverty, or of extreme poverty.
messages.lead: The Sages taught a baraita with regard to the nature of a sliding-scale offering, which varies depending on the owner’s financial status:

notes.he: גמ' עשירות כשבה או שעירה. דלות תורים ובני יונה. דלי דלות עשירית האיפה:
notes.en: GEMARA: Wealth: a female lamb or a female goat. Poverty: doves or young pigeons. Extreme poverty: a tenth of an ephah.

notes.dh: יולדת ומצורע מביאין בדלות ועשירות דהכי אשכחן בהו
notes.he: שמיעת קול וכו' מביא אף בדלי דלות. היינו עשירית האיפה דכתיב בהן. מצורע מביא בדלות:
notes.en: A woman after childbirth and a leper bring in poverty and in wealth, for so we find with them. The hearing of the voice, etc., bring even in extreme poverty, that is, a tenth of an ephah, which is written of them. A leper brings in poverty.

messages.text: A woman after childbirth brings a sliding-scale offering either in poverty, i.e., two doves or two pigeons, one as a burnt offering and one as a sin offering, or in wealth, i.e., a lamb as a burnt offering and a dove or a pigeon as a sin offering (see Leviticus 12:1–8).

A leper brings the offering either in poverty in the form of a lamb for a guilt offering, and two doves or two pigeons, one as a sin offering and one as a burnt offering, or in wealth in the form of a lamb for a guilt offering, a lamb as a burnt offering, and a female lamb as a sin offering (see Leviticus 14:10–22).

notes.he: דאידך ברייתא לאו דוקא וההיא ברייתא המוגהת דוקא ואפילו הכי אמר לי ר' מצורע מביא בדלות דמביא ב' פרידין כשהוא עני תחת ב' כבשים. והנך שתי ציפרין חיות טהורות דקא מייתי נמי עשיר הנהו לאו לכפרה אתו אלא לגרום לו טהרה:
notes.en: For the other baraita is not precise, while that corrected baraita is precise. And even so, my teacher told me: a leper brings in poverty, since when he is poor he brings two young birds instead of two lambs. And the two live, pure birds that even a rich man brings do not come for atonement, but to bring about his purification.

messages.text: For the hearing of the voice, i.e., taking a false oath that one cannot provide testimony, or the utterance of the lips, or the defiling of the Temple or its sacrificial foods, one brings an offering either in wealth, i.e., a female lamb or goat as a sin offering, or in poverty, i.e., two doves or two pigeons, one as a sin offering and one as a burnt offering, or in extreme poverty, i.e., a meal offering.

notes.dh: שמיעת הקול ובטוי שפתים וטומאת מקדש וקדשיו
notes.he: מפרש בויקרא שמביאים בדלות ובדלי דלות:
notes.en: The hearing of the voice, the utterance of the lips and the defiling of the Temple and its sacred foods: it is explained in Vayikra that they bring in poverty and in extreme poverty.

messages.text: When offerings are brought in poverty rather than wealth, there is a case in which one brings one offering instead of a different one; there is a case in which one brings two offerings instead of two other offerings; there is a case in which one brings two offerings instead of one offering; and there is a case in which one brings one offering instead of two offerings.

notes.he: מפרש לקמן:
notes.en: There are those who bring, etc.: it is explained below.

messages.text: From here you may derive that the offering of one-tenth of an ephah may be worth as little as one peruta.

A woman after childbirth brings one offering instead of one offering: One young bird, as a sin offering that she would bring even in wealth, and another bird as a burnt offering instead of the lamb. A leper brings two young birds instead of two lambs.

notes.he: בעשירות כבש לעולה ובן יונה או תור לחטאת: ובדלות שתי תורים דהיינו פרידה דעוף תחת כבש:
notes.en: A woman after childbirth: in wealth, a lamb for a burnt offering and a young pigeon or a dove for a sin offering; and in poverty, two doves, that is, a young bird instead of a lamb.

notes.he: בעניותה ומאי היא פרידה דעוף תחת כבש דבעשירותה מביאה כבש לעולה ובן יונה או תור לחטאת. ואם לא תמצא ידה די שה ולקחה שתי תורים או שני בני יונה אחד לעולה ואחד לחטאת. ומצורע מביא ב' פרידין תחת ב' כבשים שמביא בעשירותו אחד לעולה ואחד לחטאת וכבש אחד בלבד לאשם דמצורע מביא חטאת ועולה ואשם:
notes.en: A woman after childbirth brings one instead of one: in her poverty. And what is it? A young bird instead of a lamb; for in her wealth she brings a lamb for a burnt offering and a young pigeon or a dove for a sin offering, “and if her means do not suffice for a lamb, then she shall take two doves or two young pigeons, one for a burnt offering and one for a sin offering” (Leviticus 12:8). And a leper brings two young birds instead of two lambs that he brings in his wealth, one for a burnt offering and one for a sin offering, and only one lamb for a guilt offering, since a leper brings a sin offering, a burnt offering and a guilt offering.

messages.text: For the hearing of the voice and the utterance of the lips and the defiling of the Temple or its sacrificial foods, one brings two young birds instead of one female lamb, and in a case of extreme poverty one brings one meal offering of one-tenth of an ephah instead of two young birds.

notes.dh: שמיעת קול וכו' מביאין שני פרידין תחת כבשה אחת
notes.he: כדכתיב בהו:
notes.en: The hearing of the voice, etc.: they bring two young birds instead of one female lamb, as is written of them.

notes.he: דהיינו אחת תחת שתים:
notes.en: A tenth of an ephah instead of two young birds: that is, one instead of two.

messages.caption: The sliding-scale offering by means, as the two baraitot set it out: who brings what in wealth, poverty and extreme poverty, and what replaces what.

messages.text: The baraita teaches: From here you may derive that the offering of one-tenth of an ephah may be worth as little as one peruta. From where do we learn this halakha? It is as the Sages taught in a baraita:
messages.quote: one-tenth of an ephah may be worth as little as one peruta

messages.text: In the case of one who says: It is incumbent upon me to bring an offering worth one sela to the altar, he brings a lamb, as there is nothing that is sacrificed upon the altar that is worth one sela other than a lamb.

notes.he: בקרבן הנקח בסלע:
notes.en: It is incumbent upon me [to bring] a sela: an offering bought for a sela.

messages.text: From where is this halakha derived? It is derived from the fact that the Merciful One states in the Torah that the ram brought in its second year as a guilt offering must be “according to your valuation in silver by shekels” (Leviticus 5:15), i.e., it must be worth two sela. It may therefore be understood by inference that a lamb, i.e., a young ram, in its first year is worth one sela.

verse.he: נֶפֶשׁ כִּי־תִמְעֹל מַעַל וְחָטְאָה בִּשְׁגָגָה מִקׇּדְשֵׁי יְהֹוָה וְהֵבִיא אֶת־אֲשָׁמוֹ לַיהֹוָה אַיִל תָּמִים מִן־הַצֹּאן בְּעֶרְכְּךָ כֶּסֶף־שְׁקָלִים בְּשֶׁקֶל־הַקֹּדֶשׁ לְאָשָׁם׃
verse.en: When a person commits a trespass, being unwittingly remiss about any of GOD’s sacred things: They shall bring as a penalty to GOD a ram without blemish from the flock, convertible into payment in silver by the sanctuary weight, as a reparation offering.

notes.he: (מדבכל התורה כולה קרי לכבש בן שנה מכלל דאיל בן שתי שנים):
notes.en: (Since throughout the Torah it calls a lamb “in its first year,” by inference a ram is in its second year.)

notes.he: גבי אשם מעילות בויקרא איל בכסף שקלים דהיינו שתי סלעים:
notes.en: Since the Merciful One wrote: concerning the guilt offering for misuse of consecrated property, in Vayikra, a ram “in silver shekels,” that is, two sela.

notes.he: וקשה שהרי אומר בחטאת בת דנקא בפרק איזהו מקומן (זבחים דף מח.) וגם אמרינן לקמן (כריתות דף כז.) מפני מה לא נתנה תורה שיעור קצבה למחוסרי כפרה שמא יוזלו טלאים ואין להם כפרה וי"ל הא דקאמר כבש בסלע רגילות הוא שקונהו בסלע למצוה מן המובחר אבל בפחות סגי אבל אשם צריך כסף שקלים דמדאורייתא הוא אבל חטאת דאורייתא אין לה שיעור רק מדרבנן לכך מצוה לכתחלה בסלע ובפחות סגי עד דנקא אבל פחות מדנקא מיקרי עבריינא ומכל מקום אם הוזלו והם שמנים בפחות מדנקא מתכפר בהם ובאשמות אפילו הם שמנים וטובים בפחות מכסף שקלים שהוזלו אינו מתכפר משום דכתיב כסף שקלים:
notes.en: By inference, a lamb in its first year is a sela: This is difficult, for it says that a sin offering may be worth a danka (in the chapter Eizehu Mekoman, Zevaḥim 48a), and we also say below (Keritot 27a): Why did the Torah not fix a set value for those lacking atonement? Lest lambs become cheaper and they would have no atonement. One can answer: when it says a lamb for a sela, that is the usual practice, to buy it for a sela for the choicest fulfillment of the mitzva, but less is enough. A guilt offering, however, requires “silver shekels” by Torah law, whereas a sin offering has no set value by Torah law, only by rabbinic law. Therefore the mitzva at the outset is a sela, and less is enough down to a danka; one who brings less than a danka is called a transgressor. In any case, if lambs became cheaper and fat ones cost less than a danka, he gains atonement with them. But with guilt offerings, even if they are fat and good, if they cost less than silver shekels because prices fell, he does not gain atonement, since “silver shekels” is written.

notes.he: היינו מדרבנן דמן התורה אמרי' בכל דוכתא חטאת בת דנקא ועוד אמר רבי כשמביאה בסוף שנתה יביאה בסלע אבל משמיני והלאה דמא בן ח' אפי' בדנקא יביא:
notes.en: By inference, a lamb in its first year is a sela: that is by rabbinic law, for by Torah law we say everywhere that a sin offering may be worth a danka. And furthermore, Rabbi [our teacher] said: when one brings it at the end of its year, one should bring it for a sela; but from the eighth day on, at the price of an eight-day-old animal, one may bring it even for a danka.

notes.he: מעילות בערכך כסף שקלים בשקל הקדש לאשם ואיל היינו בן שתי שנים מכלל דכבש בן שנה בסלע:
notes.en: Since the Merciful One said ram for a guilt offering: [the guilt offering] for misuse, “according to your valuation in silver shekels, by the shekel of the Sanctuary, for a guilt offering”; and a ram is in its second year; by inference a lamb in its first year is a sela.

messages.text: And it is known that a lamb is brought when it is within its first year, as it is written: “A lamb of the first year” (Leviticus 12:6). And we learned in a mishna (8a):

verse.he: וּבִמְלֹאת ׀ יְמֵי טׇהֳרָהּ לְבֵן אוֹ לְבַת תָּבִיא כֶּבֶשׂ בֶּן־שְׁנָתוֹ לְעֹלָה וּבֶן־יוֹנָה אוֹ־תֹר לְחַטָּאת אֶל־פֶּתַח אֹהֶל־מוֹעֵד אֶל־הַכֹּהֵן׃
verse.en: On the completion of her period of purification, for either son or daughter, she shall bring to the priest, at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, a lamb in its first year for a burnt offering, and a pigeon or a turtledove for a purgation offering.

messages.text: The price of nests, i.e., pairs of birds brought by an impoverished person instead of a lamb, stood that day at one-quarter of a silver dinar.

notes.he:
קן ברובע דינר דהיינו כדמייתי שתי פרידים בדלות ברובע דינר תחת כבש הנקח בסלע היינו חד מט"ז בסלע שהוא ד' דינרים ורובע דינר היינו י"ו רבעים:
ברובע דינר יש מ"ח פרוטות כדאמרינן בפ"ק דקדושין (דף יב.) שש מעה כסף דינר ומעה שתי פונדיון ופונדיון ב' איסרין ואיסר ב' מסמסות מסמס ב' קונטרק וקונטרק ב' פרוטות דהיינו ל"ב פרוטות למעה ולמעה וחצי שהוא רובע דינר הוו מ"ח פרוטות וכיון דאמרת דלי דלות דהיינו עשירית האיפה בעי מהוי חד מי"ו בדלות אשתכח דעשירית האיפה הוי ג' פרוטות דהיינו חד מי"ו של מ"ח:
notes.en:
At a quarter [berova’atayim]: a nest for a quarter-dinar; that is, one brings two young birds in poverty for a quarter-dinar instead of a lamb bought for a sela, which is one-sixteenth of a sela, since a sela is four dinars, and a quarter-dinar is [one of its] sixteen quarters.
In a quarter-dinar there are forty-eight perutot, as we say in the first chapter of Kiddushin (12a): six silver ma’ah are a dinar; a ma’ah is two pundeyon; a pundeyon is two issar; an issar is two mismas; a mismas is two kontrank; and a kontrank is two perutot. That is thirty-two perutot to a ma’ah, and in a ma’ah and a half, which is a quarter-dinar, there are forty-eight perutot. And since you said that extreme poverty, which is a tenth of an ephah, must be one-sixteenth of poverty, it turns out that a tenth of an ephah is three perutot, which is one-sixteenth of forty-eight.

notes.he: ומדכתיב ביולדת תביא כבש בן שנתו דהיינו בסלע ובעניותה מביאה קינין ותנן בפרקין דלעיל עמדו קנין על שתי נשים בו ביום ברבעתים בחצי דינר היינו של אשה אחת ברובע דינר:
notes.en: And since it is written concerning a woman after childbirth, “she shall bring a lamb in its first year,” which is a sela, and in her poverty she brings nests; and we learned in our previous chapter: nests stood that day at a quarter [berova’atayim], at half a dinar, that is, for two women; so for one woman, a quarter-dinar.

messages.text: A quarter-dinar is one-sixteenth of a sela, the price of a lamb.

And from the fact that the Merciful One has mercy upon one who brings an offering in poverty, in that He permits him to bring an offering that is worth one-sixteenth of the value of the lamb that is brought in wealth, it may be inferred that the Merciful One takes pity upon one who brings an offering in extreme poverty, and consequently He permits him to bring an offering which is worth one-sixteenth of the value of the offering brought in moderate poverty. Accordingly, the offering brought in extreme poverty may be equal to a two hundred fifty-sixth part of the value of a sela.

notes.dh: ומדחס רחמנא עליה דדלות למיהוי חד מי"ו דעשירות
notes.he: דרובע דינר דעמד בו קן אשה אחת (וכל קן דעלמא) זהו י"ו בסלע דסלע הוי ד' דינרין. הכי נמי חס רחמנא עליה דדלי דלות עשירית האיפה למיהוי חד מי"ו בדלות ברובע דינר:
notes.en: And since the Merciful One had pity on poverty, that it be one-sixteenth of wealth, for the quarter-dinar at which the nest of one woman stood (and every ordinary nest) is one-sixteenth of a sela, as a sela is four dinars; so too the Merciful One had pity on extreme poverty, a tenth of an ephah, that it be one-sixteenth of poverty, of a quarter-dinar.

messages.text: If so, how much is the offering brought in poverty worth? It is worth one-quarter of a dinar. And how many perutot are in one-quarter of a dinar? Forty-eight perutot. Accordingly, how many perutot are in the offering brought in extreme poverty, which is worth one-sixteenth of the offering brought in poverty? Three perutot.
messages.lead: The Gemara examines the mathematics necessary to determine that the value of the offering brought in extreme poverty is equal to one peruta:

notes.dh: וכמה פרוטי יש ברובע דינר מ"ח
notes.he: כיצד שש מעה כסף דינר ורובע דינר מעה וחצי ומעה ב' פונדיונין היינו מעה וחצי ג' פונדיונין ופונדיון ב' איסרין היינו רובע דינר ו' איסרין ופרוטה אחד משמונה באיסר נמצא ברובע דינר מ"ח פרוטות חד מי"ו בהן היינו ג' פרוטות דיש בהן ג' פעמים י"ו פרוטות ואמאי קתני מיכן את למד לעשירית האיפה בפרוטה ג' פרוטות הוי:
notes.en: And how many perutot are in a quarter-dinar? Forty-eight. How so? Six silver ma’ah are a dinar, and a quarter-dinar is a ma’ah and a half; a ma’ah is two pundeyon, so a ma’ah and a half is three pundeyon; a pundeyon is two issar, so a quarter-dinar is six issar; and a peruta is one-eighth of an issar. So there are forty-eight perutot in a quarter-dinar, and one-sixteenth of them is three perutot, since they contain sixteen perutot three times over. So why does it teach: from here you learn that a tenth of an ephah is for a peruta? It is three perutot!

messages.text: But with regard to that which the baraita teaches: From here you may derive that the offering of one-tenth of an ephah may be worth as little as one peruta, why did the baraita teach that it may be worth one peruta, rather than three perutot? Didn’t you say that one-tenth of an ephah is brought in extreme poverty, and you also said that this offering should be worth one-sixteenth of the offering brought in poverty, which we calculated to be three perutot?
messages.quote: From here you may derive that the offering of one-tenth of an ephah may be worth as little as one peruta

notes.he: אינו כשיעור שער בינוני הנזכר בכל התלמוד ד' סאין בסלע דהוא איפה בג' דינר ושש מעה כסף דינר הרי יגיע עשירית האיפה יתר ממעה וחצי:
notes.en: A tenth of an ephah for a peruta: this does not match the average price mentioned throughout the Talmud, four se’a for a sela, which is an ephah for three dinars; and since six silver ma’ah are a dinar, a tenth of an ephah comes to more than a ma’ah and a half.

messages.text: The tanna derives the cost of an offering brought in poverty from the case of a woman after childbirth, who brings one bird instead of a lamb, as a bird is worth one thirty-second of the value of a lamb.

notes.he: דלות יליף מיולדת דמתיא פרידה הנקחת בשמינית של דינר תחת כבש הנקח בסלע דהיינו חד מל"ב בכבש והוא כ"ד פרוטות:
notes.en: The tanna derives it from a woman after childbirth: he derives poverty from a woman after childbirth, who brings a young bird bought for an eighth of a dinar instead of a lamb bought for a sela, that is, one thirty-second of the lamb, which is twenty-four perutot.

notes.he: תנא דקתני עשירית האיפה בפרוטה מיולדת יליף דמתיא בדלות פרידה אחת לעולה תחת כבש של סלע ופרידה אחת היינו חצי קן שקנו בחצי רובע דינר דהיינו חד מתלתין ותרין דסלע דכבש וקן דלות שלם הוי חד מי"ו בעשירות כדאמרן:
notes.en: The tanna who teaches a tenth of an ephah for a peruta derives it from a woman after childbirth, who in poverty brings one young bird for a burnt offering instead of a lamb worth a sela. One young bird is half a nest, bought for half a quarter-dinar, that is, one thirty-second of the sela of the lamb; and a whole nest of poverty is one-sixteenth of wealth, as we said.

messages.text: But until now, how much was the offering brought in extreme poverty calculated to be worth? One-sixteenth of the value of the offering brought in poverty. And from where is this derived? It is derived from the value of the lamb and the ram, as explained earlier. If so, until now, the calculations lead to the conclusion that the offering brought in extreme poverty is worth one and one-half perutot, as one thirty-second of the value of a lamb is equal to one-eighth of a silver dinar rather than one-quarter, which means that the offering brought in poverty is worth twenty-four perutot, one-sixteenth of which is equal to one and one-half perutot.

notes.dh: ועד כאן דלי דלות כמה הוי חד מט"ז בדלות
notes.he: דנהי דילפת דדלות חד מל"ב מיולדת אבל דלי דלות דלא משכחת ביולדת בע"כ מכבש ואיל ילפת לה כדדרשינן לה לעיל דלא משכחת דלי דלות אלא בשמיעת הקול ובבטוי שפתים ובמטמא מקדש וקדשיו וע"כ דלי דלות מדלות דידהו מילף וכי היכי דדלות דידהו שתי פרידין תחת הכבש דהיינו חד מי"ו בדלות ונהי דאשכחת בדלות בעלמא כגון ביולדת שהיא פרידה אחת שמינית של דינר דהיינו כ"ד פרוטות וכי מייתי דלי דלות חד מי"ו הוי פרוטה ופלגא:
notes.en: And until now, how much is extreme poverty? One-sixteenth of poverty: granted that you derive from a woman after childbirth that poverty is one thirty-second; but extreme poverty, which is not found with a woman after childbirth, you perforce derive from the lamb and the ram, as we expounded above. For extreme poverty is found only with the hearing of the voice, the utterance of the lips and one who defiles the Temple and its sacred foods, and perforce extreme poverty is derived from their own poverty: just as their poverty is two young birds instead of the lamb, which is one-sixteenth, [so extreme poverty is one-sixteenth] of poverty. And granted that you found poverty elsewhere, as with a woman after childbirth, which is one young bird, an eighth of a dinar, that is, twenty-four perutot; when one brings extreme poverty at one-sixteenth of that, it is a peruta and a half.

notes.he: אלא מחצי קן יליף מפרידה תחת כבש ודלי דלות כמה הוי חד מי"ו דדלות דפרידה היינו חצי רובע דינר וחצי רובע דינר יש בו כ"ד פרוטות א"כ חד משיתסר היינו פרוטה ופלגא ואמאי קתני עשירית האיפה בפרוטה:
notes.en: Rather, he derives it from half a nest, from a young bird instead of a lamb. And extreme poverty, how much is it? One-sixteenth of poverty. A young bird is half a quarter-dinar, and in half a quarter-dinar there are twenty-four perutot; if so, one-sixteenth is a peruta and a half. So why does it teach a tenth of an ephah for a peruta?

messages.text: The entire matter is derived from the offering brought by a woman after childbirth, and this is what the tanna is saying: It is derived from the fact that the Merciful One has mercy upon one who brings an offering in poverty, in that he may bring an offering which is worth one thirty-second of the value of the offering brought in wealth.

notes.he: ואע"ג דאין בה דלי דלות יליף מהתם דכי היכי דאשכחן בה דלות אחד מל"ב דעשירות דלי דלות נמי הוה חד מל"ב דדלות ודלות דיולדת הכי הוו כ"ד פרוטות ודלי דלות פרוטה נכי רבעא דהיינו חד מל"ב:
notes.en: The entire matter is derived from a woman after childbirth: even though she has no extreme poverty, it is derived from there: just as we found with her that poverty is one thirty-second of wealth, extreme poverty is also one thirty-second of poverty. The poverty of a woman after childbirth is twenty-four perutot, and extreme poverty is a peruta minus a quarter, which is one thirty-second.

notes.he: בין דלות בין דלי דלות מיולדת יליף דמביא פרידה אחת [תחת] כבש ולא קתני חד משיתסר כדאמרת אלא חד מתלתין ותרין:
notes.en: Ravina said [the daf’s text reads Rava]: The entire matter, both poverty and extreme poverty, is derived from a woman after childbirth, who brings one young bird [instead of] a lamb; and it does not teach one-sixteenth, as you said, but one thirty-second.

messages.text: And from what case is this principle derived? From the case of a woman after childbirth.

So too, the Merciful One has mercy upon one who brings an offering in extreme poverty, in that he may bring an offering that is worth one thirty-second of the value of the offering brought in moderate poverty.

notes.dh: והכי קאמר מדחס רחמנא על דלות למיהוי חד מן ל"ב בסלע
notes.he: כדאמרן דהיינו כ"ד פרוטות חס נמי על דלי דלות למיהוי חד מן ל"ב בדלות דהיינו חד מי"ו דהיינו י"ב פרוטות ושיתסר מי"ב פרוטות היינו פרוטה נכי ריבעא:
notes.en: And this is what it says: since the Merciful One had pity on poverty, that it be one thirty-second of a sela, as we said, which is twenty-four perutot, He also had pity on extreme poverty, that it be one thirty-second of poverty, which is one-sixteenth of twelve perutot; and one-sixteenth of twelve perutot is a peruta minus a quarter.

messages.text: Rabbeinu Gershom reads Ravina here, where the daf’s text reads Rava.
If so, the value should be one peruta minus one-quarter, i.e., three-quarters of a peruta.

notes.he: נמצא עשירית האיפה פרוטה נכי ריבעא:
notes.en: If so: a tenth of an ephah turns out to be a peruta minus a quarter.

messages.text: Indeed that is so, but it is not proper conduct to bring an offering worth less than one peruta before God.

notes.he: אין הכי נמי ובציר מפרוטה הוי והאי דקתני מיכן לעשירית האיפה בפרוטה דלאו אורח ארעא לאייתויי פחות מפרוטה למקדש:
notes.en: Indeed, it is less than a peruta; and the reason it teaches, “from here [you learn that] a tenth of an ephah [is] for a peruta,” is that it is not proper conduct to bring less than a peruta to the Temple.

messages.caption: Three ways to price the tenth of an ephah: by the lamb and the ram (three perutot), the tanna’s bird from the woman after childbirth (one and a half), and Rava’s whole derivation from her (three-quarters of a peruta, though one does not bring less than a peruta before God).

messages.text: Mishna

What are the differences between an espoused maidservant and all those others with whom relations are forbidden? The difference is that the status of the maidservant is not equal to their status, neither with regard to punishment nor with regard to an offering,

notes.he: מה בין שפחה לבין כל העריות כו' לא בעונש שכל העריות או במיתת ב"ד או בכרת וכאן במלקות:
notes.en: What is [the difference] between a maidservant and all those with whom relations are forbidden, etc.: not with regard to punishment, for all those with whom relations are forbidden are [punished] either by court-imposed death or by karet, while here it is by lashes.

messages.text: as one who unwittingly engages in intercourse with any of those with whom relations are forbidden is liable to bring a sin offering, and by contrast, one who unwittingly engages in intercourse with an espoused maidservant is liable to bring a guilt offering. One who unwittingly engages in intercourse with any of those with whom relations are forbidden brings a female animal, and one who unwittingly engages in intercourse with an espoused maidservant brings a male animal, as a sin offering is a female and a guilt offering is a male.

notes.he: מתני' כל חטאת יחיד נקבה היא דהיינו כשבה או שעירה:
notes.en: MISHNA: Every sin offering of an individual is a female, that is, a female lamb or a female goat.

messages.text: Furthermore, with regard to engaging in intercourse with any of those with whom relations are forbidden, both the man and the woman are equal with regard to liability to receive lashes if they were forewarned, and with regard to liability to bring an offering if they did so unwittingly.

notes.he: אם מזידין שניהן לוקין כדקיי"ל איש או אשה כי יעשו מכל חטאת האדם וגו' השוה הכתוב אשה לאיש לכל העונשין ואם שוגגין שניהם מביאין קרבן דבתרווייהו כתיב כרת במזיד דכתיב ונכרתו הנפשות העושות וכל שזדונו כרת שגגתו חטאת:
notes.en: Equal with regard to lashes and an offering: if both acted intentionally, both are flogged, as we hold: “When a man or woman shall commit any sin” (Numbers 5:6): the verse equated a woman to a man for all punishments. And if both acted unwittingly, both bring an offering, since for both of them karet is written for the intentional act, as it is written: “And the souls that do them shall be cut off” (Leviticus 18:29), and anything whose intentional violation is punishable by karet requires a sin offering for its unwitting violation.

notes.he: וכל העריות בזכר דמחויב בין זכר בין נקבה והשפחה בנקבה ולא בזכר דאין חיוב בעבד:
notes.en: And with all those with whom relations are forbidden, [both are equal] with regard to the male, since both the male and the female are liable; but the maidservant is liable with regard to the female and not with regard to the male, for there is no liability for the slave.

messages.text: And in the case of one who engages in intercourse with a maidservant, the Torah did not equate the man with the woman with regard to lashes, as she alone is flogged, as will be explained, and the Torah did not equate the woman with the man with regard to bringing an offering, as she does not bring an offering.

notes.he: שהאשה לוקה והאיש באשם כדמפרש בגמ':
notes.en: And with a maidservant, etc.: the woman is flogged and the man brings a guilt offering, as explained in the Gemara.

messages.text: With regard to intercourse with any of those with whom relations are forbidden, the Torah rendered the halakhic status of one who engages in the initial stage of intercourse [hame’areh] to be like that of one who completes the act, and one is liable to bring a sin offering for each and every act of intercourse that he performs unwittingly. By contrast, in the case of relations with an espoused maidservant, one is liable only for completing the act of intercourse, and the man brings a single offering for several transgressions.

notes.dh: כל העריות כולן עשה בהן מערה כגומר
notes.he: במסכת יבמות בפרק הבא על יבמתו (יבמות דף נג:):
notes.en: With all those with whom relations are forbidden, it rendered the initial stage like completion: [this is taught] in tractate Yevamot, in the chapter HaBa al Yevimto (Yevamot 53b).

notes.he: ובשפחה אינו חייב אלא על גמר ביאה דשכבת זרע כתיב בה שראויה להזריע:
notes.en: And with a maidservant, one is liable only for completing the act of intercourse, since “lying of seed” is written concerning her [Leviticus 19:20], [that is, intercourse] that can lead to conception.

notes.dh: וכל העריות חייב על כל ביאה וביאה
notes.he: ובשפחה אמרו לעיל בפירקין (כריתות דף ט:) שמביא קרבן אחד על ביאות הרבה:
notes.en: And with all those with whom relations are forbidden, he is liable for each and every act of intercourse: but concerning a maidservant they said earlier in our chapter (Keritot 9b) that he brings one offering for many acts of intercourse.

notes.he: מה שאין כן בשפחה שמביא קרבן אחד על ביאות הרבה:
notes.en: And he is liable for each and every act of intercourse: which is not so with a maidservant, for he brings one offering for many acts of intercourse.

messages.text: This is a stringency that the Torah imposed with regard to the maidservant relative to other individuals with whom relations are forbidden:
Continues on 11a: the mishna goes on to say that the Torah established that one who engages in intercourse with her intentionally is like one who does so unwittingly.
